text: Pulse is the living energy every Tribal Power machine runs on. Generators make it, machines spend it, and a **Pulse Cell** lets you carry some in your pocket for tools, spells and travel.

pages.title: Where Pulse lives
text: Pulse is stored energy. A generator such as the Drumheart, the Ley Collector or the Pulse Resonator makes it and keeps it in its own store. A machine reaches out and spends it while it works.

Machines only look **8 blocks** around themselves. Pulse stored in a generator farther away, or in an unloaded chunk, cannot help. For your first workshop, simply put the generator right beside the machine. A line of Lattice Conductors, each within 8 of the next, extends that same reach.
Machines drain nearby generators first, then stores such as the totem buffers a [Lattice Conductor](lattice_conductor) fills (each Resonance Totem holds **250 Pulse**) and Pulse Cairns.

pages.title: Supply and demand
text: A machine can run for a while from a reserve even when it spends faster than you generate. If it keeps starting and stopping, compare the Pulse it needs with what your generators make, then add generation or build a bigger reserve.

Totems are not generators. A matching totem gives a station its voice, called **attunement**; it does not make power. Crouch and right-click a machine with this book and it reports power and attunement separately.

steps.caption: A charged Drumheart holds the Pulse you drummed into it.
Right-click it with a Pulse Cell: one use fills the cell as far as the drum holds.
A Pulse Resonator, a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp, or a Pulse Cairn fills a cell the same way, all it can take in one use.
The generator loses what the cell gains. A Ley Collector cannot fill a cell this way.

pages.title: Carrying it
text: A Pulse Cell holds **1,200 Pulse**; a **Greater Pulse Cell** holds **4,800**; a **Grand Pulse Cell** holds **19,200**. Carry charged cells for spells, Spiritgear, charms and travel, which all draw on cells in your inventory.
A cell in your pocket is **not** a nearby generator. Workshops and tablet rites still need Pulse within 8 blocks of them.
To pay for a Way Gate, use a cell on its keystone (up to **100** per use); the trip spends that store, not the cell in your pocket. A Gate Drum needs no Pulse at all: its rite opens it.
A [Pulse Gauge](pulse_gauge) pointed at a machine that holds Pulse reads how full it is.
